To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mesoporous silica-coated iron oxide nanoparticles are a promising support for the immobilization of lipase, and the hybrid response surface methodology-genetics algorithm (RSM-GA) approach is a powerful tool for the optimization of ultrasound-assistant transesterification reaction of WCO.
immobilized lipase can be successfully used for the synthesis of FAMEs from waste oil, and the optimum conditions for FAME synthesis were found by using hybrid RSM-GA optimization.
the immobilized lipases on mesoporous iron oxide/silica core-shell nanoparticles could be used for the synthesis of biodiesels from waste cooking oil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient, environmentally benign and cost-effective process for the production of biodiesel.
the synthesis of magnetic nanoparticles as a novel support material for the immobilization of lipase and the optimization of biodiesel production using the RSM-GA hybrid method.
the development of immobilized lipase as a catalyst for the synthesis of biodiesels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a new and promising strategy for biodiesel production from WCO using a superparamagnetic mesoporous silica-Fe3O4 core-shell nanoparticles as an immobilized support.

this work is the first report of using mesoporous silica coated superparamagnetic iron oxide as an immobilization substrate for lipase and its application for biodiesel production by transesterifying waste cooking oil.
the hybrid RSM-GA method could provide a useful tool for optimization of the biodiesel production process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mesoporous silica-coated superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles are an effective substrate for lipase enzyme immobilization.
the immobilized lipases on the core-shell nanoparticles could be a promising biocatalyst for the biodiesel synthesis.
the hybrid RSM-GA optimization approach is a powerful tool for the prediction of FAME content in enzymatic transestrification of WCO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immobilized lipases are promising catalysts for transesterification reaction of WCO to produce biodiesel.
a superparamagnetic core-shell nanoparticle can be used as an efficient substrate for lipase enzyme immobilization.
the immobilized lipases can be reused for several times without loss of activity and can be easily separated from the reaction medium by using an external magnetic field.
